speaker: Unknown
en: Bezos at Amazon, it's customer obsession.
zh: Bezos 在 Amazon 的时候,讲的是顾客痴迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in our mind, that's an input metric.
zh: 但在我们看来,那是一个输入指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to measure input metrics.
zh: 你不应该去衡量输入指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter if you're customer obsessed.
zh: 你是不是痴迷顾客并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could be customer obsessed and they file a restraining order against you because they don't like what it is that you're doing.
zh: 你可以很痴迷顾客,然后他们因为不喜欢你在做的事而对你申请限制令。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our job is to build something so good that our customers themselves become obsessed with us.
zh: 我们的工作是把东西做得足够好,好到我们的顾客自己反过来痴迷于我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is our job.
zh: 这才是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: The analogy is, if you're a coach of a basketball team,
zh: 打个比方,如果你是一支篮球队的教练,

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to tell your players before they come out there like, hey guys, make sure to sweat.
zh: 你不会在球员上场之前跟他们说:嘿,伙计们,记得要流汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, what?
zh: 那感觉就像是,什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no, like score points.
zh: 不对,是要得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we need to score points.
zh: 我们需要得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in doing so, yeah, you're probably going to sweat.
zh: 而在这么做的过程中,是的,你很可能会流汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think similarly to create obsessed customers, you probably need to be really obsessed yourself with the customers, but the output is what matters.
zh: 我认为同样的道理,要创造出痴迷的顾客,你自己很可能确实需要对顾客非常痴迷,但重要的是输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're here in the studio with Matan from Factory.
zh: 我们今天在演播室里请到了来自 Factory 的 Matan。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is our second time with Matan.
zh: 这是我们第二次请到 Matan。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, indeed.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 感谢邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're here in the small and elite group of second-time training data attendees, so thank you.
zh: 我们现在是第二次来做客 training data 的小而精英的群体的一员了,谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 哦,是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Matan is the co-founder and CEO of Factory, which makes droids, which are autonomous agents for the art of software development.
zh: Matan 是 Factory 的联合创始人兼 CEO,Factory 做 droids,也就是用于软件开发艺术的自主智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, indeed.
zh: 是的,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Matan, we're going to jump right in because I think you guys are a little bit of a dark horse candidate in this world of software development.
zh: Matan,我们要直接进入正题了,因为我觉得你们在软件开发这个领域里有点像黑马候选者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a market that has absolutely taken off.
zh: 这是一个已经彻底起飞的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are folks like Claude Code and Cognition and others who have a lead, but you guys are coming up strong.
zh: 有像 Claude Code 和 Cognition 这样的玩家已经领先,但你们正在强势追赶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about the competitive dynamics and what makes Factory special.
zh: 谈谈竞争态势,以及是什么让 Factory 特别。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a wild ride.
zh: 这是一段疯狂的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started Factory three and a half years ago now.
zh: 我们在三年半前创立了 Factory。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in April of 2023, when the world and the enterprise in particular was barely ready
zh: 也就是 2023 年 4 月,当时世界、尤其是企业,连

speaker: Unknown
en: For GitHub Copilot, let alone fully autonomous agents.
zh: GitHub Copilot 都还没准备好接受,更不用说完全自主的智能体了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the first two years, it was kind of our journey in the desert is how I like to refer to it, because we were focused on fully autonomous agents, but engineers weren't ready.
zh: 所以我认为头两年,有点像我喜欢说的「旷野中的旅程」,因为我们专注于完全自主的智能体,但工程师们还没准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Procurement teams at the enterprise weren't ready.
zh: 企业的采购团队也没准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so.
zh: 所以呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think retrospectively, we really like honed our craft and learned a lot about how to build for developers in the enterprise.
zh: 回头看,我们真的磨练了自己的手艺,学到了很多关于如何为企业的开发者构建产品的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, it took a lot of time to actually come around to when they were ready to receive it.
zh: 但是,你知道,等他们真正准备好接受的时候,确实花了很多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're kind of now emerging much more.
zh: 所以我们现在算是更活跃地崭露头角了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of these other players like Anthropic or OpenAI who have a ton of distribution are going in and bringing their incredible tools like Claude Code or Codex.
zh: 而其中一些其他玩家,比如 Anthropic 或 OpenAI,他们拥有大量的分发渠道,他们带着自己令人惊叹的工具进来,比如 Claude Code 或 Codex。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that enterprises are really caring about that we have learned through those two years is they do not want anyone to kind of be their single point of failure.
zh: 我们在这两年中学到的一点是,企业真正在意的,是他们不希望任何人成为自己的单点故障。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do not want anyone to kind of control their fate.
zh: 他们不希望任何人掌控自己的命运。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so something that really matters is model independence.
zh: 所以真正重要的一件事是模型独立性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone learned from cloud where, you know, back in the cloud days, it was like AWS or Azure being like, hey, you know, come on in, sign this three-year contract.
zh: 所有人都从云身上学到了教训,你知道,在云的时代,AWS 或 Azure 会说:嘿,来吧,签这份三年的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be so cheap.
zh: 会非常便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to subsidize it.
zh: 我们会补贴的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be great.
zh: 会很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a couple of years later, when it came time to renewal, they would 10X the contract.
zh: 然后几年之后,到了续约的时候,他们会把合同价格提高十倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Haha, data gravity, we got you now.
zh: 哈哈,数据引力,我们现在拿捏你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we got you.
zh: 是啊,我们拿捏你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you going to do, a two-year migration to go to someone else?
zh: 你能怎么办,花两年时间迁移到别家去?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no way.
zh: 不可能吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone has scars from that now.
zh: 现在每个人都带着那段经历留下的伤疤。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so everyone knows, look, Claude Code is fantastic.
zh: 所以大家都知道，Claude Code 非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Codex from OpenAI is fantastic.
zh: OpenAI 的 Codex 也非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We cannot put our fate in any one of these model providers' hands.
zh: 我们不能把自己的命运交到任何一家模型提供商的手里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, like, you just look at the risk profiles of
zh: 而且，你只要看看风险画像就能发现，

speaker: Unknown
en: The Model Labs versus the cloud providers.
zh: 模型实验室和云提供商是不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the last piece of drama that came out of one of the cloud providers versus like the Model Labs?
zh: 云提供商最近一次爆出的丑闻，和模型实验室相比如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like there's kind of always some sort of chaos of internal fighting or getting in spats with the government or any other entities.
zh: 似乎总是有某种内部斗争的混乱，或者和政府或其他实体发生争执。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're going to build this very important part of your business, you want to make sure that you're robust to any of these changes.
zh: 所以如果你要构建业务中这么重要的一部分，你要确保自己对任何这些变化都有韧性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something that we've learned over those kind of initial two years is like,
zh: 这也是我们在最初那两年里学到的东西，就是，

speaker: Unknown
en: Developers really care about things being modular.
zh: 开发者真的非常在意模块化。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to know that they can customize it to what they want.
zh: 他们想知道自己可以按自己的需求进行定制。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to know that if there's a new model that comes out that's faster or cheaper or more performant, they can kind of hot swap it in.
zh: 他们想知道，如果有新的模型出来，更快、更便宜或性能更好，他们可以热插拔地把它换进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's, I think, one of the biggest reasons why a lot of the largest enterprises are taking the momentum that they had from a Codex or a Claude Code and then are carrying that into factory because they get that performance from these fantastic models, but they do it without the vendor lock-in that, you know, the ModelLabs directly
zh: 我认为这是很多最大型企业把从 Codex 或 Claude Code 上获得的势头延续到 Factory 的最大原因之一，因为他们从这些出色的模型中获得性能，却没有你 ModelLabs 直接带来的那种厂商锁定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I'm the enterprise, I'm going to be like, wait a minute, am I now just getting locked into factory?
zh: 而如果我是企业方，我会说，等等，我现在是不是只是被锁定在 Factory 上了？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the answer to that?
zh: 对这个问题的回答是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a really good question because that is something that you might think of like, okay, wait, so we're just switching the lock-in point.
zh: 这是个非常好的问题，因为你可能会想，好，等等，我们只是换了一个锁定点而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of the modularity that we build is such that if at some point you wanted to say, hey, you know what?
zh: 我们构建的所有模块化设计，都是为了如果某一天你想说，嘿，你知道吗，

speaker: Unknown
en: Factory is not staying at the frontier anymore, whether it's like the automations that you build or the skills registry that we help you create.
zh: Factory 不再保持在前沿了，无论是你构建的自动化流程，还是我们帮你创建的技能注册表。

speaker: Unknown
en: The work that we've done stays in your code base and any of the automations that we've created, the artifacts also live in your code base.
zh: 我们所做的工作都留在你的代码库里，我们创建的任何自动化流程，这些产物也存在于你的代码库中。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, there aren't really things that we're saying like our tribal knowledge about your org that we're keeping on our side and not giving to you.
zh: 换句话说，并没有什么东西是我们所说的，比如关于你们组织的、我们所谓的内部专有知识，被我们扣在自己这边不给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's part of the relationship that we have with customers is like, we similarly want to make sure we're providing the best experience possible.
zh: 这也是我们与客户关系的一部分，就是，我们同样希望确保自己提供尽可能最好的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we help you arbitrage between different models to get cost optimization, we're giving you that optimization.
zh: 如果我们帮你在不同模型之间做套利以实现成本优化，我们是把那个优化给你的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not taking that away from you.
zh: 我们不会把它从你那里拿走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's a really important part of the trust that we're building with these enterprises.
zh: 我认为这是我们与这些企业之间建立的信任中非常重要的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You and I were talking probably a couple months ago at this point, and I was trying to give you credit for having the right vision for this market two, three years ago.
zh: 你和我大概在几个月前聊过，我当时试图称赞你，说你在两三年前就对这 个市场有了正确的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you responded with something along the lines of, thank you, but being two or three years early is the same as being wrong.
zh: 而你回应的大意是，谢谢你，但早了两三年和错了是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which I thought was a wonderful response in so many ways.
zh: 我觉得这个回答在很多方面都非常精彩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk about like that, those two years in the desert, how did it feel to have this vision that turned out to be right, that nobody appreciated?
zh: 你能谈谈那两年在荒野中的经历吗？当你拥有这个最终被证明正确、却没人欣赏的愿景时，是什么感觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: For a year or two.
zh: 持续了一两年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just talk about like that journey and what it has done to the DNA of your company?
zh: 你能谈谈那段历程，以及它给你们公司的 DNA 带来了什么影响吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, in the moment, it's really, really difficult because, you know, I hadn't had a job before.
zh: 我是说，在当时，那真的非常非常艰难，因为，你知道，我之前从来没工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I dropped out of my PhD to start this company.
zh: 我从博士退学来创办这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, over the course of those two years, convinced, you know, 20 of the smartest people that I've ever met to quit what it was that they were doing and, you know, join factory and join us on this mission.
zh: 而且，你知道，在那两年里，我说服了我见过的最聪明的二十个人，让他们辞掉手头的工作，加入 Factory，加入我们这项使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are people with families.
zh: 而这些人有家庭。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are people with kids who are like dedicating years of their lives to this problem and going, you know, customer after customer.
zh: 这些人有孩子，他们把生命中的数年奉献给这个问题，然后一家接一家地拜访客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they like they weren't ready for agents.
zh: 而他们，他们那时候还没准备好接受智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't get it.
zh: 他们没理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the models weren't as performant, but I think a lot of it was behavioral.
zh: 另外，当时的模型性能也没那么好，但我认为很大程度上是行为层面的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, even just a fun anecdote of like giving developers an NPS survey.
zh: 我是说，甚至有个有趣的轶事，就是给开发者做 NPS 调查。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you ever are giving a developer an NPS survey, they do not like whatever it is that you're giving it to them.
zh: 如果你给开发者做 NPS 调查，无论你给他们什么，他们都不喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because like developers, they vote with their feet.
zh: 因为开发者是用脚投票的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are very clear what they like and what they don't like.
zh: 他们非常清楚自己喜欢什么、不喜欢什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're like, hmm, I wonder if they like it.
zh: 如果你在想，嗯，不知道他们喜不喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: They definitely don't.
zh: 他们肯定不喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And but during that time, I think there were there was a lot that we were learning.
zh: 不过在那段时间里，我觉得我们学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a lot that I myself was like, I'd never had a job before.
zh: 有很多是我自己也，我之前从来没工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enterprise sales is not something that comes obvious to a physicist.
zh: 企业销售不是一个物理学家天生就会的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the end of the day, it doesn't it doesn't matter.
zh: 但说到底，这都不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no you don't get any bonus points for being early.
zh: 早到是没有任何加分项的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because who cares?
zh: 因为谁在乎呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there's no consolation prize.
zh: 就是没有安慰奖这回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's either you do the thing or you don't do the thing.
zh: 要么你把这件事做了,要么你没做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's all that matters.
zh: 这才是唯一重要的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for the team is really tough.
zh: 而对团队来说真的很难熬。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were points where we ended up getting good at enterprise sales, but the product still wasn't good.
zh: 有几个阶段我们最终变得擅长企业销售了,但产品仍然不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a very tricky position to be in because we ended up, you know, getting to a point where we were like just under 2 million in revenue and the product was not good.
zh: 这是一个非常尴尬的处境,因为我们最后到了一个地步,收入刚好不到 200 万美元,而产品并不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was a point in time where we realized this because if you're really good at sales, you can sign contracts.
zh: 曾有一段时间我们意识到了这一点,因为如果你真的很擅长销售,你能签下合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like you can definitely do that.
zh: 就像你肯定能做到那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're doing that and the developers don't like your product, it's like a ticking time bomb because it's eventually they're going to turn and it's going to be really, really bad.
zh: 但如果你在这么做,而开发者不喜欢你的产品,那就像一颗定时炸弹,因为最终他们会流失,而且会变得非常非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: We realized this.
zh: 我们意识到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we proactively gave all of those customers their money back.
zh: 于是我们主动把所有这些客户的钱退了回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember that was one of the most difficult decisions to make, because not only is there a group of 20 people who are getting ridiculous offers from all the labs, they have these huge financial incentives to go elsewhere, there are all these other companies that are doing well, and they decided to do this.
zh: 我记得那是最艰难的决定之一,因为不仅有 20 个人这一群体正收到来自各大实验室的离谱offer,他们有巨大的经济激励去别处,还有这么多其他公司做得很好,而他们决定这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we're going to say, oh, yeah, hey, by the way, that, you know, a little bit of revenue we managed to get, we're actually going to give it back because we don't think product is making their developers happy.
zh: 然后我们还要说,哦,是的,嘿,顺便说一下,我们好不容易拿到的那么一点收入,我们其实要退回去,因为我们认为我们的产品没有让他们的开发者满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also had to tell... Why did you make that decision?
zh: 我们还不得不告诉……你们为什么做那个决定?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we sold them on a good vision and convinced them that, you know, this is the right team to work with and that we were going to deliver the solution for them.
zh: 你知道,我们向他们兜售了一个美好的愿景,说服他们相信我们是合适的合作团队,我们会为他们交付解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we realized that the way that we had sold them on it and the product that we were delivering was not up to snuff in a way that I don't think...
zh: 但我们意识到,我们兜售它的方式与我们实际交付的产品并不达标,以至于我不认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: It would hold true to one of our operating principles.
zh: 它会符合我们的一条运营原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of our operating principles that I really like is create obsessed customers.
zh: 我们有一条我非常喜欢的运营原则,就是打造痴迷的客户(create obsessed customers)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This kind of like flips over Bezos's thing where Bezos at Amazon, it's customer obsession.
zh: 这有点像把贝索斯的那个说法翻转过来,贝索斯在亚马逊讲的是客户至上(customer obsession)。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in our mind, that's an input metric.
zh: 但在我们看来,那是一个输入指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And input metrics are like, you don't want to measure input metrics.
zh: 而输入指标嘛,你不会想去衡量输入指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter if you're customer obsessed.
zh: 你是否痴迷于客户并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you could be customer obsessed and they file a restraining order against you because they don't like what it is that you're doing.
zh: 就像你可以痴迷于客户,然后他们因为你做的事对你申请限制令。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like our job is to build something so good that our customers themselves become obsessed with us.
zh: 我们的工作是打造出足够好的东西,好到客户自己对我们着迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is our job.
zh: 那才是我们的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, you know, the analogy is if you're a coach of a basketball team, you don't want to tell your players before they come out there like, hey, guys, make sure to sweat.
zh: 就像,你知道,类比是,如果你是一支篮球队的教练,你不会在球员上场前告诉他们,嘿,伙计们,记得要出汗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, what?
zh: 那就像,什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, no, like score points.
zh: 就像,不,去得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we need to score points.
zh: 我们需要得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in doing so, yeah, you're probably going to sweat.
zh: 而在这么做的过程中,是的,你很可能会出汗。

zh: 而且让我们非常明确。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the signals, the inputs that we are taking in here.
zh: 这些就是我们在这里接收的信号、输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, great.
zh: 好，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have those signals.
zh: 我们有了那些信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then what is the process by which we build this?
zh: 那么我们构建它的流程是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And really like mapping out the like assembly lines of how you are building software is really important because then...
zh: 真正地把你的软件组装流水线画出来是非常重要的，因为那样的话……

speaker: Unknown
en: You get to close the loop and say, did this actually deliver outcome for our business?
zh: 你就能闭环，说：这真的为我们的业务带来了成果吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Talking before about the tokenomics, if you're that CIO and you're faced with that question of where do you put every incremental token, really the question two years from now is going to become where do you put every incremental dollar?
zh: 之前谈到过 tokenomics，如果你是那个 CIO，面对“每一个增量 token 放在哪里”这个问题，那么两年后真正的问题会变成“每一个增量美元放在哪里”？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're going to have to be asked, do you put that incremental dollar towards headcount or towards tokens?
zh: 所以你会被迫回答：你是把增量美元投给人力，还是投给 token？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if tokens, to where in the org?
zh: 如果是 token，投给组织里的哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are things that you can only really know when you have these kind of feedback loops that give you examples of like, hey, by the way, we made those decisions based on this data.
zh: 而这些只有当你拥有这种反馈循环、给你类似“嘿，顺便说一下，我们当时是基于这些数据做那些决策的”这样的例子时，才能真正知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it did not matter at all.
zh: 而结果发现那根本不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We added these new features and no one cared.
zh: 我们加了这些新功能，但没人在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't create more retention.
zh: 它没有带来更多留存。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't create more usage or whatever metrics that business is looking to optimize.
zh: 它没有带来更多使用量，或者该业务想要优化的任何指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the only way to do this is like you need kind of more rigor and more process.
zh: 而做到这一点的唯一方式就是你需要更多的严谨性和更多的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: It almost feels like like 10 years from now, we're going to look back at this previous era of software and it's going to feel like businesses in like ancient times where they didn't do accounting.
zh: 感觉就像十年后，我们回望之前这个软件时代，它会像古代那些不做会计的企业一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be like marketing in the day of Mad Men, where it's like all creative and you have no idea what's actually working.
zh: 会像《广告狂人》那个年代的营销，全靠创意，而你完全不知道什么真正有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes no sense.
zh: 毫无道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's like, oh, yeah, let's ship that feature.
zh: 比如，“哦，耶，我们发布那个功能吧。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I think it went well.
zh: “哦，我觉得它做得不错。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, yeah, I got some metrics on that.
zh: “耶，我拿到了一些指标。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, no, if you guys read the blog post that Jack Dorsey put out about how every company is like an AGI.
zh: 就像，“不，如果你们读过 Jack Dorsey 发的那篇博客，说每家公司都像一个 AGI。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also this degree to which, if your company is an AGI, you want to optimize the weights.
zh: 还有一点就是，如果你的公司是一个 AGI，你会想优化权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to figure out what nodes are doing what things, which are load-bearing, which are not, which need more tokens, where do you need more nodes?
zh: 你想弄清楚哪些节点在做什么事情，哪些是承重的，哪些不是，哪些需要更多 token，哪里需要更多节点？

speaker: Unknown
en: And in order to do that, you don't train a model by vibes.
zh: 而要做到这一点，你不能凭感觉训练模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, okay, actually, you kind of do.
zh: 我是说，好吧，其实你确实有点是凭感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't, I guess more importantly, you don't do back prop in a model by vibes.
zh: 你不会——我想更重要的是——你不会凭感觉对一个模型做反向传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you are running those actual like calculations and you are seeing when we change this node, what happens.
zh: 就像你是在运行那些实际的计算，你在看当我们改变这个节点时会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you might be making bets on how to change the model by vibes, but you like, you're, it's pretty like mathematical in what you were doing.
zh: 现在你可能在凭感觉做如何改变模型的押注，但你正在做的事情是相当数学化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, at companies, you know, people are determining token budgets just by shooting from the hip.
zh: 与此同时，在公司里，你知道，人们只是在拍脑袋决定 token 预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are laying people off by shooting from the hip and just being like, oh yeah, like 20,000.
zh: 人们在拍脑袋裁员，就说，哦 yeah，比如两万人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no way there is science to laying off 20,000 people.
zh: 裁掉两万人这件事不可能有什么科学依据。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is just like, here's a chunk and let's just see what happens.
zh: 那就只是，这里砍一块，然后看看会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, I think in these organizations, the way they can do things is much more mathematical of like...
zh: 相反，我认为在这些组织里，它们做事的方式可以更数学化一些，比如……

speaker: Unknown
en: This part of the business matters a lot and does better if we give it more tokens.
zh: 这部分业务非常重要，如果我们给它更多 token，它会做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't actually matter if we give it more humans.
zh: 即使我们给它更多人，其实并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's give them more tokens.
zh: 所以让我们给它更多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: There might be other parts of the business where actually giving them more tokens doesn't matter, but more people matter because if we build more relationships with our customers and deeper relationships with our customers, that matters.
zh: 可能还有其他部分业务，给它们更多 token 其实不重要，但更多的人重要，因为如果我们与客户建立更多、更深入的关系，那很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But these are things that we're going to need like quantitative insight on and you need a software factory to do that.
zh: 但这些是我们需要定量洞察的事情，而你需要一个软件工厂来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Otherwise, you're just like shooting from the hip and just guessing, which won't work as well.
zh: 否则，你就只是在拍脑袋瞎猜，那样效果不会那么好。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the limit, how much do you think people will spend on tokens versus on engineering account?
zh: 在极限情况下，你觉得人们会在 token 上花多少，相对于在工程账户上花多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll depend on the business.
zh: 这取决于业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every business will have a balance and it just depends on like, look, they're just going to be like, an easy example is generally salespeople, they probably don't need that many tokens if they're good salespeople.
zh: 我认为每项业务都会有自己的平衡，这取决于——你看，一个简单的例子是，通常来说销售，如果他们是好的销售，他们可能不需要那么多 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because generally where they provide the most alpha is like when they're in the seat face to face with their customers, talking about the customer's problems, understanding how they build software in our case and how we can make that more efficient, more productive.
zh: 因为通常来说，他们提供最大 alpha 的地方是当他们坐在位置上、面对面与客户交流时，谈论客户的问题，理解在我们的案例中他们如何构建软件，以及我们如何能让这更高效、更有生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can use tokens a little bit of like, oh, whatever, generate them some, you know, AI debrief, take some notes, like help them with the follow up.
zh: 他们可以少量使用 token，比如，哦，随便，帮他们生成一些，你知道的，AI 简报，记一些笔记，比如帮他们做后续跟进。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like that's so minimal, the number of tokens, it basically doesn't matter.
zh: 但像那样 token 的数量少到基本无所谓。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you add more tokens to the sales team, it probably won't change their output.
zh: 就像如果你给销售团队更多 token，可能不会改变他们的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you add more humans to the sales team, it probably will.
zh: 如果你给销售团队增加更多的人，可能会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meanwhile, engineering teams are pretty different, where engineering teams, generally, it seems like you want people to own an outcome end to end, but then if you give them more tokens, they can produce a lot more.
zh: 与此同时，工程团队就很不一样，工程团队通常来说，你似乎希望人们对一个结果端到端负责，但如果你给他们更多 token，他们能产出多得多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it seems like there, and then there's a lot of kind of places in between of like operations, finance, marketing.
zh: 所以在那里似乎是这样，然后还有很多介于两者之间的地方，比如运营、财务、市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are places where are neither here nor there, where I think they're somewhere in between and it kind of depends on your business.
zh: 这些地方哪边都不算，我认为它们处于中间某处，这在一定程度上取决于你的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think every business is going to have to ask, like, what is our core competency?
zh: 但我认为每项业务都将不得不问，比如，我们的核心竞争力是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that we see a lot in the market, or we used to see, and now they finally kind of hit reality.
zh: 这是我们在市场上经常看到的，或者说过去常看到的，现在他们终于有点撞上现实了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we used to see is, oh, like, we're going to build our own, like, software development agents.
zh: 我们过去看到的是，哦，比如，我们要构建自己的，比如，软件开发智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, okay, like, you're a, like a consumer, like, logistics company.
zh: 然后我们说，okay，比如，你是一个，比如一家消费级物流公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you sure you want to do that?
zh: 你确定你想这么做吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, yeah, we have to do this.
zh: 他们说，yeah，我们必须这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, okay.
zh: 然后就是，okay。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then six months later, it's like, wait, actually, this is not a core competency for our business.
zh: 然后六个月之后，就是，等等，其实，这不是我们业务的核心竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to hire, you know, AI engineers to be doing this.
zh: 我们不想雇，你知道的，AI 工程师来做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our core competency is, you know, consumer logistic.
zh: 我们的核心竞争力是，你知道的，消费级物流。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what we want to focus on.
zh: 那才是我们想专注的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is an opportunity for every business to double down on their core competency and what matters for them and then procure externally whatever it is that doesn't matter for them.
zh: 我认为这对每项业务来说都是一个机会，去加倍押注它们的核心竞争力和对它们重要的事情，然后对外采购那些对它们不重要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a trivial example of this is like,
zh: 一个微不足道的例子是，

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, in the days of the early internet, you probably had to be a programmer to build a website.
zh: 我不知道，在早期互联网时代，你可能得是个程序员才能建一个网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like websites generally help if you're a pizza shop because you want to have, you know, people come to your pizza shop, they want to be able to or like whatever.
zh: 而且网站通常对披萨店有帮助，因为你想让人们来你的披萨店，他们要能，或者随便什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: At that time, would you say it was a core competency of like a pizza shop to have engineers?
zh: 在那个时候，你会说拥有工程师是披萨店的核心竞争力吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like certainly not like that is kind of a byproduct of like a brief moment in time.
zh: 肯定不是，那只是某个短暂时刻的副产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there were companies out there that help you build a website.
zh: 但后来出现了帮你建网站的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to be technical.
zh: 你不需要懂技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then this is why we live in a world where like most pizza shops don't have an engineering department, which I think is probably a good thing.
zh: 这就是为什么我们生活在这样一个世界里，大多数披萨店没有工程部门，我认为这大概是件好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think similarly, a lot of businesses have dealt with the reality of if you want to do X, Y, Z other thing, you have to bring in people of this type of role.
zh: 而我认为类似地，很多企业都面对过这样的现实：如果你想做 X、Y、Z 之类别的事情，你就得引入这种类型角色的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that's been like something you had to do, not because it's a core competency of the business.
zh: 但我认为那是你不得不做的事，并不是因为它是业务的核心竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And allowing businesses to focus and double down on the things that they are best at, I think is going to be good for the consumers of their business.
zh: 而让企业能够专注于并加倍押注它们最擅长的事情，我认为对它们的消费者来说会是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think we're just going to see like a lot like ruthless refocusing on what actually matters, which is going to be cool to see.
zh: 所以我认为我们只会看到很多，比如，对真正重要的事情进行无情重新聚焦，那会很值得一看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, on that, so, you know, every company kind of has to go through this process of reinvention.
zh: 嗯，说到这个，你知道，每家公司都多少得经历这个再造过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, 10 or 20 years ago, people talked about digital transformation.
zh: 你知道，10 年或 20 年前，人们谈论数字化转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't know if anybody's given it a buzzword now, but AI transformation, something of that sort.
zh: 我不知道现在有没有人给它起了个流行词，但 AI 转型，大概是这类说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: A couple of years ago, you ran into a bunch of organizations that just weren't ready to deal with autonomous agents.
zh: 几年前，你会遇到一堆根本没准备好应对自主智能体的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things you've seen your customers start to change.
zh: 你看到你的客户开始发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question is,
zh: 所以问题是，

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at your customers as they kind of go up this maturity curve and sort of reinvent themselves for the future, any good like tricks or techniques that you've seen them use to repot themselves a bit?
zh: 当你看着你的客户沿着这条成熟度曲线往上走、为未来重塑自己时，你见过他们用什么好用的技巧或方法来给自己“换个盆重新栽”一下？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think surprisingly like the companies that have been doing like company-wide hackathons
zh: 是的，我的意思是，令人惊讶的是，那些搞全公司范围黑客马拉松的公司

speaker: Unknown
en: Really end up doing well.
zh: 最终真的做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like relatively trivial, but like just setting aside a day where everyone in the workforce is just like build shit with AI.
zh: 看起来相对微不足道，但就是留出一天，让所有员工就用 AI 造点东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really sets the tone and sets the pace.
zh: 这真的定下了基调，定下了节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just give me a look.
zh: 那么让我给你看看。

speaker: Unknown
en: I tried to force him to build stuff with coding agents.
zh: 我试着强迫他用编程智能体造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't go so well.
zh: 结果不太顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll work on it.
zh: 我们会继续努力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll do it after this.
zh: 我们结束后就做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we gave it a great effort.
zh: 你知道，我们已经很努力了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's it.
zh: 但就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It literally just setting aside the time to do it.
zh: 真的就是留出时间去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if it fails miserably, it's fine.
zh: 即使失败得很惨，也没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also the orgs that are okay with failing.
zh: 还有那些能接受失败的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like there are some who are like, we need to do it exactly right.
zh: 感觉有些组织是这样的：我们必须做得完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to make the right decision from day one.
zh: 我们必须从第一天起就做出正确的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to make mistakes.
zh: 你会犯错误的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone is going to.
zh: 每个人都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the orgs who are kind of leaning into it and embracing it to a certain degree, I think are succeeding.
zh: 而那些在某种程度上拥抱它、接受它的组织，我认为正在成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of our largest customers is EY.
zh: 我们最大的客户之一是 EY。

speaker: Unknown
en: EY is not necessarily known to be at the absolute frontier of AI, but I think for them, they were just like, look, this matters.
zh: EY 不一定被认为处于 AI 的绝对前沿，但我想对他们来说，他们就是：听着，这件事很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have been other transformations that we relate to.
zh: 曾经有过其他我们能感同身受的转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to be late to this.
zh: 我们不会在这件事上迟到。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just going to go in.
zh: 我们就是要直接进场。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might mess up, but obviously respecting the things that you're not allowed to mess up, put those aside.
zh: 我们可能会搞砸，但显然要尊重那些不允许搞砸的事情，把那些放到一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go and get our engineers to mess around and build this stuff and see where it breaks and understand what they like and what they don't like.
zh: 让我们的工程师去随便折腾、造这些东西，看看它会在哪里出问题，了解他们喜欢什么、不喜欢什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that really matters a lot in the ones that we're seeing succeed and also the ones who are like,
zh: 我觉得这在我们看到的成功案例中真的很重要，还有那些

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty bold in reinventing the processes that they've put in place.
zh: 在重塑他们已建立的流程方面相当大胆的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just saying like, hey, there's no sacred cows, like, let's put this aside, try something out.
zh: 就是说：嘿，没有什么是神圣不可动的，让我们把这个放到一边，试一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it doesn't work, put that sacred cow right back.
zh: 如果不奏效，就把那头圣牛放回原处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's been kind of a determining factor there.
zh: 我认为这在那里是一个决定性因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when it comes from within.
zh: 而且当它来自内部时。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it comes from the board, probably not gonna go well.
zh: 如果来自董事会，可能不会顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it comes from within, like, the tech team or the ICEs or the leadership, that's when we see it go better.
zh: 如果来自内部，比如技术团队、ICE 或领导层，那我们看到的就会更顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have any predictions for the most important changes that are going to happen in your space in the next, call it 12 months?
zh: 对于未来，比如说 12 个月内，你所在领域将要发生的最重要的变化，你有什么预测吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of AI consumption is going up like crazy and everyone's super, super excited because the revenue is going wild.
zh: 大量 AI 消耗正在疯狂上涨，所有人都超级超级兴奋，因为营收在疯涨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a lot of this is synchronous usage.
zh: 但其中很多是同步使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, like if everyone woke up sick tomorrow, like a lot of Claude code usage would be zero.
zh: 换句话说，如果明天所有人都病倒了，很多 Claude Code 的使用量会变成零。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's all just, hey, Claude Code, or hey, Codex, or hey, Droid, right?
zh: 因为全都是：嘿，Claude Code，或者嘿，Codex，或者嘿，Droid，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in 12 to 24 months, like 90% of tokens will be asynchronous tokens.
zh: 我认为在 12 到 24 个月内，90% 的 token 将是异步 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are going to be, you know, droids on their own autonomously being like, hey, here's some signal that I found from a customer, let's go fix it, or let's go create a first pass solution to this.
zh: 所以这些将会是，你知道，droid 自己自主地运作，比如说：嘿，我发现了一个来自客户的信号，我们去修一下，或者我们去做一个初步方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is going to be where...
zh: 我认为那将会是……

speaker: Unknown
